einstellungen.text: Six out of ten done. Or four out of ten missing. Same thing. Right?
One day until the opening. You've painted your progress on the wall.
Ten boxes for ten stations. Six of them are green. The clock over the door ticks loudly.
"Four stations missing. We'll never make it."
You're talking about the same progress. And you sound like two different worlds. Eda crosses her arms. So do you.
You write both sentences on two notes. Smooth index cards. Side by side.
One note scares you. The other calms you down. And nothing has changed. Nothing at all.
In nineteen eighty-one, two researchers showed that the same options, worded differently, can change decisions.
Ms. Sen walks by. She only asks, "What does each station cost?"
You write down the hours. And what each station really gives visitors. Suddenly the studio goes quiet.
Two stations you can finish tonight. Two you cut. No drama. No guilt.
Eda slides the two notes on top of each other. They match perfectly.
The scary version and the calm version describe exactly the same six stations.
